results.text: System MUST allow users to create photo albums, each with a user-provided name.
Users MUST be able to add photos from their library to an album.
System MUST keep albums separate: a photo belongs to at most one album at a time, and adding a photo that is already in another album requires the user to confirm moving it.
System MUST display all albums on the main page, grouped by album creation date (most recent group first).
Users MUST be able to reorder albums within a date group on the main page via drag and drop.
System MUST persist the user's custom album order so it is retained across sessions.
System MUST NOT allow an album to be placed inside another album; dropping an album onto another album reorders them side by side and never creates nesting.
System MUST display the photos of an opened album as a grid of uniform tiles.
Users MUST be able to open an individual photo from its tile into a larger single-photo view and return to the tile grid.
Each album entry on the main page MUST show the album name, its photo count, and a representative cover image (most recently added photo by default).
Users MUST be able to rename an album, delete an album (with confirmation), and remove individual photos from an album.
Deleting an album or removing a photo from an album MUST NOT delete the underlying photo from the user's library.
System MUST persist albums, photo-to-album assignments, and ordering so the user's organization survives closing and reopening the app.
System MUST show an appropriate empty state for an album with no photos and for a main page with no albums, each prompting the relevant next action.
A first-time user can create a new album and add their first photos to it in under 1 minute.
Users can locate and open a specific album from the main page in under 10 seconds, even with 50+ albums present.
Opening an album of up to 500 photos presents a browsable tile grid within 2 seconds.
Album order set by drag-and-drop is retained in 100% of subsequent sessions, and no sequence of drag-and-drop actions can ever produce a nested album.
90% of first-time users complete the core flow (create an album, add photos, reorder albums) without assistance.
System MUST allow a registered user to create a short link from a valid destination URL.
System MUST validate submitted destination URLs and reject malformed or unsupported ones with a descriptive error message.
System MUST generate a unique short code for each link when no custom alias is provided.
System MUST redirect any visitor of an active short link to its destination URL without requiring the visitor to sign in.
Users MUST be able to optionally specify a custom alias when creating a link, subject to an allowed character set and length limits.
System MUST reject a custom alias that is already in use or matches a reserved word, and MUST inform the user why.
System MUST record each click on a short link, including at minimum the time of the click.
Users MUST be able to view the total click count and clicks-over-time breakdown for each link they own.
System MUST restrict link management and statistics visibility to the link's owner — no user may view or modify another user's links.
Users MUST be able to set an optional expiration date/time on a link at creation, and to add, change, or remove it later.
System MUST stop redirecting an expired link and instead show visitors a page explaining that the link has expired.
Users MUST be able to list, deactivate, and delete their own links; a deactivated or deleted link MUST stop redirecting.
System MUST show a "not found" page for short codes that do not exist, without revealing whether a code ever existed.
System MUST retain a link's accumulated statistics after the link expires or is deactivated, until the link is deleted by its owner.
A user can go from submitting a long URL to having a working short link in under 30 seconds.
Visitors following an active short link reach the destination in under 1 second in 95% of cases.
Click statistics visible to the owner reflect at least 99% of actual clicks, and appear in the dashboard within 1 minute of the click.
Expired links stop redirecting within 1 minute of their expiration time in 100% of cases.
90% of first-time users successfully create a short link (with or without a custom alias) on their first attempt without external help.
The service sustains 1,000 concurrent redirect requests without visitor-facing errors or degradation.

System MUST accept a path to a web server access log file and parse entries in the common access log formats (Common Log Format and Combined Log Format), extracting at minimum: timestamp, requested endpoint, and response status.
System MUST report the top endpoints ranked by request count, showing the count and share of total traffic for each; the number of endpoints shown MUST default to 10 and be configurable.
System MUST compute and report error rates: overall percentage of failed requests, split into client errors (4xx) and server errors (5xx), and the endpoints with the highest error counts.

System MUST detect traffic spikes in a log file by comparing request volume per time window against the surrounding baseline, and report each spike's time range, request count, and magnitude relative to baseline.
System MUST tolerate malformed lines by skipping them, and MUST report how many lines were skipped; it MUST NOT abort the whole analysis because of individual bad lines.
System MUST provide a watch mode that continuously follows a log file, processing new entries as they are appended.

In watch mode, System MUST raise an alert when an anomalous condition is detected, covering at minimum: error rate in the recent window exceeding a threshold, and request volume deviating sharply from the established baseline.
Alerts MUST be delivered to the operator's terminal, clearly distinguishable from normal output, and MUST include what condition fired, when, and the observed value versus the threshold or baseline.
In watch mode, System MUST survive log rotation and truncation of the watched file, resuming from the new file/beginning without terminating.
System MUST allow the operator to configure analysis and alerting parameters, at minimum: spike sensitivity, error-rate alert threshold, and the time window size used for rate calculations.
System MUST support restricting batch analysis to a user-specified time range.
System MUST offer the summary report in both a human-readable form and a machine-readable structured form suitable for consumption by scripts.
System MUST use exit codes that distinguish successful analysis, analysis completed with warnings (e.g., skipped lines above a notable share), and failure (unreadable file, unrecognized format).
System MUST be able to analyze log files significantly larger than available memory without failing.

An operator can go from a raw log file to a complete summary report (top endpoints, error rates, spikes) with a single command, with results for a 1 GB file available in under 60 seconds on typical operator hardware.
On reference log files with independently verified contents, reported endpoint counts and error rates match the ground truth exactly (100% agreement).
In watch mode, an alert for an anomalous condition appears within 30 seconds of the triggering entries being written to the log.
Under normal (non-anomalous) traffic replayed over 24 hours, watch mode raises no more than 2 false alerts.
Analysis completes successfully on log files containing up to 10% malformed lines, and the report accurately states the number of lines skipped.
An operator unfamiliar with the raw log format can answer "what are the top 5 endpoints and the overall error rate?" from the report alone on their first attempt, without consulting the raw log.
System MUST allow shoppers to enter a discount code during checkout and apply it to the current order after validation.
System MUST support percentage discount codes that reduce the eligible order subtotal by a configured percentage (1–100%).
System MUST support fixed-amount discount codes that reduce the eligible order subtotal by a configured monetary amount, capped so the merchandise total never falls below zero.
System MUST enforce an expiry date per code and reject expired codes at both application time and order placement.
System MUST enforce a per-customer usage limit per code, counting completed orders per customer, and reject applications beyond the limit.
System MUST support an optional total redemption cap per code across all customers and reject applications once the cap is reached.

System MUST enforce combination rules: each code is marked either combinable or exclusive; an exclusive code cannot be applied together with any other code, and only codes marked combinable may stack.
System MUST display each applied discount as an itemized line (code and amount saved) and show the updated order total before payment is taken.
System MUST re-validate all applied codes (active status, expiry, usage limits, combination rules) at order placement, and reject the order with a clear explanation if any code is no longer valid.
Shoppers MUST be able to remove an applied code before payment, restoring the undiscounted total.

Marketing users MUST be able to create discount codes via an admin screen, specifying: code string, discount type (percentage or fixed amount), value, expiry date, per-customer usage limit, optional total redemption cap, and combinability.
Marketing users MUST be able to deactivate (and reactivate) codes; deactivation takes effect immediately for new applications and does not alter completed orders.
System MUST enforce uniqueness of code strings (case-insensitive) and match shopper-entered codes case-insensitively with surrounding whitespace ignored.
System MUST record every redemption (code, customer, order, discount amount, timestamp) so that usage limits can be enforced and marketing can review code usage.
Access to the discount code admin screen MUST be restricted to authorized marketing/admin roles.

System MUST present distinct, shopper-friendly rejection messages for each failure reason: unknown code, expired, deactivated, per-customer limit reached, total cap reached, and not combinable with an applied code.
A shopper can apply a valid discount code and see the updated order total within 2 seconds, without leaving the checkout flow.
100% of orders placed with a discount reflect a discount amount consistent with the code's definition, and no completed order has a negative merchandise total.
Zero orders are completed using a code that was expired, deactivated, or over its usage limit at the moment of order placement.
A marketing user can create and publish a new discount code in under 3 minutes without engineering involvement.
At least 95% of shoppers who attempt to apply a code either succeed or receive a message identifying the specific reason for rejection on the first attempt.
System MUST accept temperature and vibration telemetry readings reported by registered factory floor sensors.
System MUST record for each reading: the sensor identifier, reading type (temperature or vibration), measured value with unit, and the time of measurement.

System MUST validate incoming readings and reject those that are malformed (missing fields, non-numeric values, unknown reading type), recording each rejection with a reason without interrupting ingestion of other readings.
System MUST record readings received for unregistered sensor identifiers as rejected, retaining enough detail for later investigation, and MUST NOT store them as normal telemetry.
System MUST persist accepted readings and allow operators to retrieve them by sensor and time range.
System MUST retain stored readings for at least 12 months.
Operators MUST be able to define an alert threshold per sensor and per reading type, consisting of an upper limit, a lower limit, or both.
Operators MUST be able to view, update, and remove existing thresholds; changes MUST take effect for readings received after the change.
System MUST evaluate every accepted reading against the active threshold for its sensor and reading type, and create an alert when the value falls outside the configured limits.
System MUST notify the responsible operators when a new alert episode begins, including the sensor, reading type, measured value, violated threshold, and time of breach.

System MUST group consecutive violating readings from the same sensor and reading type into a single alert episode and MUST NOT send a separate notification for each violating reading within an episode.
System MUST mark an alert episode as resolved when a subsequent reading for that sensor and reading type returns within the threshold, recording the resolution time.
System MUST record the delivery outcome of each notification so that failed deliveries are visible and auditable.
Operators MUST be able to view alert history, filterable by sensor and time range, including breach start, peak value, threshold in effect, and resolution time.
A reading reported by a sensor is visible to operators within 10 seconds of being received.
Operators are notified within 60 seconds of a threshold-violating reading being received.
An operator can configure a new threshold for a sensor in under 2 minutes.
The system ingests sustained telemetry from 1,000 sensors reporting every 10 seconds (≈6,000 readings/minute) with zero loss of valid readings.
During a continuous breach, operators receive exactly one notification per alert episode rather than one per violating reading.
100% of rejected readings (malformed or unknown sensor) are traceable in rejection records — no telemetry is silently discarded.
Users MUST be able to set a notification level per channel, choosing at minimum: all messages, mentions only (includes direct @-mentions of the user), or muted.
System MUST apply a workspace-wide default notification level to any channel the user has not explicitly configured, and users MUST be able to change their personal default.
Users MUST be able to define a recurring daily quiet-hours window (start time and end time, evaluated in the user's local time zone), including windows that span midnight.

System MUST suppress delivery of notifications during the user's quiet hours, except for keyword alerts (see FR-007), and MUST preserve suppressed activity as unread/missed items visible after the window ends.
Users MUST be able to create, view, edit, and delete a personal list of alert keywords.
System MUST match alert keywords against message content case-insensitively on whole-word boundaries.

System MUST deliver keyword-alert notifications immediately, overriding per-channel settings (including muted channels), quiet hours, and digest mode, and MUST indicate which keyword triggered the notification.
Users MUST be able to enable or disable digest mode and select a digest delivery interval from a predefined set of options.

While digest mode is enabled, system MUST hold non-urgent notifications and deliver them as a single summary per interval, grouped by channel with message counts; urgent notifications (direct messages, @-mentions of the user, keyword alerts) MUST still be delivered immediately.
System MUST NOT deliver an empty digest when no non-urgent notifications accumulated during the interval.
System MUST apply notification preference changes to all messages received after the change takes effect, without requiring the user to sign out or restart.
System MUST persist all notification preferences per user so they apply consistently across the user's sessions and devices.
When digest mode is disabled with undelivered held notifications, system MUST surface those pending notifications to the user rather than discarding them.
When a single message triggers multiple notification reasons (e.g., a mention that also matches a keyword), system MUST deliver at most one notification for that message.
A user can configure a channel's notification level, quiet hours, or a keyword alert in under 1 minute each without documentation or assistance.
100% of messages matching a user's alert keywords produce an immediate notification, regardless of channel mute, quiet hours, or digest state, in scenario testing.
Zero notifications are delivered during a user's quiet-hours window in scenario testing, excluding keyword alerts.
Users with digest mode enabled experience at least an 80% reduction in individual notification interruptions during a typical workday compared to the same activity without digest mode.
Keyword-alert and mention notifications are delivered within 5 seconds of the message being posted under normal load.
Within one month of release, support requests related to unwanted or missed notifications decrease by 30%.
